title: Hydrogen atoms in n = 2 against stellar temperature
caption: N₂/N₁ = (g₂/g₁)e^{−ΔE/k_BT} with ΔE = 10.2 eV and g₂/g₁ = 4. At 10 000 K, k_BT = 0.862 eV and N₂/N₁ = 4e^{−11.8} = 2.9 × 10⁻⁵: tiny, yet enough to show Balmer lines. The curve is steep: doubling the temperature to 20 000 K multiplies the fraction by 372.
alt: Graph of N2/N1 in units of 10^-5 against temperature in thousands of kelvin: a very steep rising curve, 2.9 at 10 000 K.
description: The horizontal axis is temperature in thousands of kelvin; the vertical axis is N₂/N₁ in units of 10⁻⁵.
The curve is 4 e^{−ΔE/k_BT}; the activation-like energy ΔE/k_B = 118366 K, so it is extremely sensitive to T.
